item.title: reports: per account and currency totals
item.brief: In the reports Python repo, change the CSV reader and totals as the shared contract specifies: accept the new `date,account,amount_cents,currency` CSV and the old one without currency (treat as USD); output `account,currency,total_cents` sorted by account then currency; malformed currency code -> stderr error, exit 2. Add unittest coverage and keep `python3 -m unittest` passing. Update README. Commit in this repo with the operator's configured git identity.

state.summary:
Implemented per-account, per-currency totals in the reports repo on archon/pkyqjntk-reports-per-account-and-currency-totals, committed as a1cd20d (not pushed). reports.py now reads the optional currency column (missing means USD), sums per (account, currency), and prints account,currency,total_cents sorted by account then currency. A malformed currency code (anything but exactly three uppercase ASCII letters, including empty) prints an error naming the account to stderr, writes nothing to stdout, and exits 2. README documents the format and error behaviour. Checks: `python3 -m unittest` passes 4/4 on the final head (tree 2b35d9c1df3ef488b84e31c93c7b6eb209037199). Before: the currency was ignored, so EUR and USD rows were summed together (rent,-120100) and a malformed `eur` was accepted. Independent review (agt_01M88PSCPN8N0F20XT0HP7PBBV) passed the commit with no blocking findings. Open follow-ups, non-blocking: (1) a row with a missing amount_cents raises an uncaught TypeError (pre-existing, unchanged); (2) the malformed-currency test does not assert the account name the README promises. Nothing is left running. Risk is high: the CLI output header changes, so any caller parsing the old account,total_cents output will break.

evidence.caption: Two EUR/USD rows for rent. Before: currency ignored and summed together. After: split by currency.
Malformed lowercase currency 'eur'. Before: accepted, exit 0. After: stderr error, exit 2, no stdout.

pr.body: Approach: reports.py reads row['currency'] (defaulting to USD when the column is absent), validates it with fullmatch on [A-Z]{3}, and keys totals by (account, currency). render() sorts the keys. A MalformedCurrency error is caught in main(), printed to stderr, and returns exit 2 with no stdout. Files: reports.py, test_reports.py, README.md. Tests: 4 unittest cases cover the sorted multi-currency output, the old currency-less CSV (USD), malformed codes (usd, EURO, E1R, EU, empty) each exiting 2 with no stdout, and a missing currency value exiting 2. Result: 4/4 OK. Review: independent reviewer passed a1cd20d with no blocking findings. Non-blocking follow-ups: a missing amount_cents still raises an uncaught TypeError (pre-existing); the malformed-currency test does not assert the account name. Assumptions: an empty currency cell in a file that has the column is malformed (exit 2), not USD. Output header change is a CLI break for callers parsing account,total_cents.
pr.summary: made reports totals per account and currency. now reads optional currency column (missing = USD) and prints account,currency,total_cents sorted by account then currency; malformed currency exits 2. before: currency ignored, EUR and USD summed together (rent,-120100), malformed codes accepted; now: rent,EUR,-120000 and rent,USD,-100 kept separate.

risk.why: Changes the CLI output header and row shape (account,total_cents becomes account,currency,total_cents with one row per currency), which breaks callers that parse the old output. Touches reports.py, test_reports.py and README.md; behaviour changes, not just tests. Tests pass 4/4; reviewer independently rated high and passed with no blocking findings.

item.title: ledger: currency column and validation
item.brief:
In the ledger Rust repo, implement the currency behaviour in the shared contract: optional 4th TSV column (ISO 4217, three uppercase ASCII letters, default USD), CSV header `date,account,amount_cents,currency`, every row gets its currency. Malformed currency -> stderr message naming the line number, exit status 2; other input errors keep exit 1. Add tests for the new behaviour and keep `cargo test` passing. Update README. Commit in this repo with the operator's configured git identity; no attribution lines beyond the commit trailer rules.

pr.body:
Approach: parse_line returns Result<Entry, ParseError>, where ParseError is Input (exit 1) or Currency (exit 2). parse_currency checks exactly 3 uppercase ASCII bytes. Missing 4th field -> DEFAULT_CURRENCY (USD). Key files: src/lib.rs, src/main.rs, tests/ledger.rs, README.md. Checks: cargo test 10/10 pass; clippy -D warnings clean. Reviewer agt_01M88PT6XMKE977ERKKBCRTMWX passed ba3cf5e with no blocking findings.

Assumptions and limits: an empty 4th column is rejected (exit 2), not defaulted. The amount error takes precedence over the currency error when both are bad. The public parse_line signature changes (library callers must handle ParseError). The sibling reports repo must accept the 4-column CSV before release.

Follow-ups (non-blocking): tests for whitespace around the currency and CRLF input; document the empty-column and check-order behaviour; fmt drift on base in is_iso_date and parse_cents.
